distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.

ensemble.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.
ensemble.rule: fraction_achieved is the share of draws in which the criterion holds. A design that achieves its function in a minority of draws has NOT achieved it: when fraction_achieved < 0.5 the status below is "not met" however the single deterministic run came out.

model_honesty.statement: STUDIO-FINDINGS.md's one honest sentence applies to everything above: every numeric wild-type value that lands in band is read straight from the paper it is scored against. The negative controls (a zebrafish that cannot glide, a wingless flying fish that cannot glide, a TFF that cannot pay for powered flight) are the part of this result that is NOT circular, because they turn on inequalities between independently sourced quantities rather than on a fitted number.

result.scope: Whether the design DOES the function asked of it, measured by running the engine's own scenario modules. It is not a validity claim and it is not a statement that the design is biologically possible: lean_check says no law is broken (necessary, not sufficient) and this says the function is or is not achieved in the model. Every check carries the validation status of the model behind it, and a check whose model is `circular` -- scored against a number read back from the paper it is compared with -- is not evidence however green it looks. The ensemble is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION over stated input distributions, most of whose shapes are assumed; it is not a measured distribution of real behaviour. Control, flapping, unsteady aerodynamics, take-off power, adhesion and whole-body stability are not modelled anywhere in this engine.

species_gate.note: the species matches the flier gate but the STAGE does not: the 15-20 m/s taxi band is measured for ADULT flying fish only; the engine's own launch speed for this STATE is not sourced (scenarios/glide.mjs organismLaunchSpeed), so no launch-speed spread is drawn and none is invented. The spread below comes only from mass, area and the wave terms.

ensembles.note: A spread computed from assumed distributions is an UNCERTAINTY ILLUSTRATION, not a measured distribution of real glides. No one has published a distribution of flying-fish glide ranges, and this ensemble is not one. What each input contributes: MEASURED spread -- the reference (lifting) area, from three Park & Choi 2010 specimens (n = 3, stuffed, one species). MEASURED-SECONDHAND band -- the 15-20 m/s launch airspeed, quoted from Davenport 1994 in two fetched sources; the band is theirs, the uniform shape inside it is ours. BORROWED -- the body-mass CV (measured on 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini, applied to a Cypselurus hiraii base mass) and the take-off path-angle sd (measured as a body-pitch sd, used as a path-angle sd, which params.json says is a different quantity). ASSUMED -- the entire sea state (the repository has none, and wind.mjs says wave effects are not modelled), so both wave terms; the gust sd, which is half of wind.mjs's own assumed design input; and the glide angle-of-attack spread. Two further limits: mass and fin area are drawn INDEPENDENTLY because no source in the repository gives their correlation, and real fish correlate them, so the wing-loading spread here is WIDER than a real population's; and the shape of every distribution is assumed, so the 5th and 95th percentiles are much softer than the median.

distributions.label: Launch (take-off) airspeed
distributions.applies: adult flying fish and the flying-fish-derived designed fliers only
distributions.source: Band 15-20 m/s, second-hand but quoted in two fetched sources: "taxiing ... can probably accelerate the flying fish to a speed up to 15 - 20 m s-1 (Davenport 1994)" (Deng, Wang, Zhang, Mao 2019, bioRxiv doi:10.1101/765560, Introduction); flying fish "glide for up to 50 m ... at an air speed of 15 to 20 m s-1" (Makiguchi et al. 2013, Aquat Biol 18:105, doi:10.3354/ab00494, Introduction, citing Edgerton & Breder 1941 and Davenport 1990); see sim-engine/scenarios/glide.mjs TAXI_END_M_S / TAXI_MAX_M_S and physics/glide-data.csv. The BAND is measured-secondhand. The UNIFORM SHAPE inside the band is ASSUMED: neither source gives a distribution, only the two endpoints. Note the simulator's own deterministic take-off target, params.json takeoff_speed_target_m_s = 17.5 (kind assumed), is the midpoint of this band, so the band is centred on the deterministic run by construction; glide.mjs instead takes 15, the band's lower end, so glide.mjs's single number is this ensemble's lower edge, not its median.

distributions.label: Flight-path angle at take-off (before the wave slope is added)
distributions.source: sd 3.3 deg is MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 3, pitch at leap 20.0 +- 3.3 deg (10 leaps, 13 fish, captive; doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Using it as the spread of the FLIGHT-PATH angle is BORROWED, and params.json says why it is not the same quantity: "the measured 20 deg (Makiguchi 2013) is the body pitch at the moment of leaping, not the path". The MEAN is the simulator's own approach_angle_deg / glide_alpha_deg geometry, not drawn here. The normal shape is assumed; the source gives a mean and an sd, not a distribution.

distributions.label: Wave-induced launch height (sea-surface elevation at take-off)
distributions.source: Added to the launch height. sigma = Hs/4, which is the DEFINITION of significant wave height for a narrow-band Gaussian sea (a standard relation, not a repository source). Hs itself is ASSUMED (SEA_STATE: 1.0 m); the repository contains no sea state and wind.mjs states "no wave-induced updrafts (not modelled)". The only measured height anchor nearby is the 8 m maximum recorded flight HEIGHT (Deng et al. 2019 Introduction, second-hand, physics/glide-data.csv), which bounds height aloft, not launch height. The repository's own launch height, glide.mjs LAUNCH_HEIGHT_PARAM = 1 m, is itself labelled assumed.

distributions.label: Sea-surface slope at take-off (added to the path angle)
distributions.source: Linear deep-water sinusoid of amplitude Hs/2 and wavelength lambda sampled at a uniformly random phase: maximum slope atan(pi Hs / lambda), rms that over sqrt(2). The GEOMETRY is standard; both inputs (SEA_STATE Hs 1.0 m, lambda 30 m) are ASSUMED, so this whole quantity is assumed. The fish leaves a sloping, moving water surface; wind.mjs does not model this at all.

distributions.label: Wind component along the flight path (positive = headwind)
distributions.source: Mean = conditions.headwind_m_s if the host supplies one, otherwise 0 (no headwind is added silently). sd = half the gust amplitude. BOTH numbers come from sim-engine/scenarios/wind.mjs, where headwind_m_s (default 5) and gust_m_s (default +-2) are labelled kind "assumed", source "design input"; wind.mjs also notes the gusts are treated quasi-steady with no unsteady aerodynamics and no shear. So this is assumed on assumed. Its only measured neighbour is Hertel's calculated 10 m/s headwind case (physics/glide-data.csv, row_kind "theory"), which is a model result, not an observed wind.

distributions.label: Body mass (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 8.70% = 19.8 / 227.7 g, MEASURED: Makiguchi et al. 2013 Table 1, body mass 227.7 +- 19.8 g over 13 Cheilopogon heterurus doederleini (doi:10.3354/ab00494, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Applying that CV to the simulator's Cypselurus hiraii base mass is BORROWED (a different genus, and captive fish). Park & Choi's own five specimen masses (0.06, 0.05, 0.06, 0.04, 0.04 kg) are rounded to 0.01 kg, so their quantisation is as large as their spread and they cannot give a usable CV. Lognormal shape is assumed; a mass must stay positive, which is the only reason that shape was chosen over a normal.

distributions.label: Aerodynamic reference (total lifting) area (specimen-to-specimen)
distributions.source: CV 2.17%, MEASURED on three specimens: Park & Choi 2010 Table 1 models L1, L2 and L3, reference area A1+A2+A3 (pectoral + pelvic + body planform) = 0.013049, 0.013243, 0.012688 m2 (doi:10.1242/jeb.046052, transcribed in physics/glide-data.csv). Models M and N are excluded because their fins were folded (A2 recorded as 0). n = 3 stuffed museum specimens of ONE species: a real measured spread, but a very small sample. span_m is scaled by the square root of the area factor so the aspect ratio, and therefore the ground-effect ratio h/(span/2), stays self-consistent. Lognormal shape assumed (area must stay positive).

distributions.label: Angle of attack held in the glide
distributions.source: Fully ASSUMED. params.json: "the fish's chosen angle of attack in the glide is not measured; the literature cited by Park and Choi says only that glides are nearly parallel to the surface". sd 2 deg is a deliberately NARROW choice representing "the fish does not hold one exact angle"; it is NOT the simulator's slider range for this parameter (-5 to 30 deg), which would dominate every other input. Set `distributions` without this entry to switch it off.
